title: Kathakali classical dance-drama
culturalContext: Kathakali is a classical dance-drama native to Kerala, characterised by intricate facial expressions (navarasas), elaborate make-up categories, and symbolic hand gestures (mudras) codified from ancient performance treatises. Performances dramatise narratives from Indian epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata. Actors undergo extensive physical training from a young age within traditional institutions and guru-shishya lineages.

title: Kasavu handloom textile of Kerala
culturalContext: Kasavu refers to the traditional off-white handloom cotton textile of Kerala featuring characteristic golden metallic or zari borders. Deeply rooted in Kerala festivals such as Onam and Vishu, the craft has protected Geographical Indication (GI) status in historic weaving centres including Balaramapuram, Chendamangalam, and Kuthampully. Traditional weavers preserve specific pit-loom techniques passed down through artisan weaver families.

title: Theyyam ritual dance of North Malabar — Panchuruli
culturalContext: Theyyam is a sacred ritual dance-form native to the Kolathunadu (North Malabar) region of Kerala, encompassing Kannur and Kasaragod districts. Performers belong to designated traditional communities who undergo strict spiritual vows and ritual preparation before adorning vibrant headgear (mudi), intricate face painting, and sacred ornaments to invoke divine presence. Panchuruli Theyyam represents a fierce protective deity worshipped in ancestral sacred groves (kavus) and village shrines across northern Kerala.

title: Aranmula Kannadi — handcrafted metal alloy mirror
culturalContext: Aranmula Kannadi is a rare front-surface metal alloy mirror handcrafted in the heritage village of Aranmula in Pathanamthitta district, Kerala. Unlike standard secondary-surface glass mirrors where light reflects from a silvered backing, the Aranmula mirror produces reflection directly from its polished bronze surface, eliminating secondary optical distortion. The secret metallurgical composition of copper and tin has been preserved across generations by a collective of traditional metalsmith families belonging to the Vishwakarma community. It received India's first craft Geographical Indication (GI) status in 2003.

title: Nettipattam — traditional elephant caparison craft
culturalContext: Nettipattam is an elaborate golden forehead ornament and ceremonial caparison crafted for temple elephants during prominent festival processions (puram) across Kerala, most famously the Thrissur Pooram. The ornament is hand-stitched by skilled artisans onto heavy cotton and woollen felt backings, mounted with hundreds of copper and brass crescent-shaped domes (bubbles or bublos) electroplated with gold. Symbolically, the arrangement represents the pantheon of Hindu cosmology, with the creator Brahma, preserver Vishnu, and destroyer Shiva positioned along the central axis, surrounded by deities of celestial directions.

title: Kerala temple mural painting — Thodeekalam
culturalContext: Kerala mural paintings represent an ancient visual art tradition dating from the 8th century CE, preserved on the walls of temples and historic palaces across Kerala. Executed in the fresco-secco method onto lime-plastered laterite surfaces, murals are painted strictly using Panchavarna (five natural mineral and herbal pigments): yellow (yellow ochre), red (red ochre), green (extracted from the leaves of the Neelamari plant or Eravikkara), white (lime), and black (oil-lamp soot). The Thodeekalam Shiva Temple in Kannur features 16th-century murals depicting complex compositions from the epics, characterized by expressive stylized eyes, rhythmic drapery, and traditional iconographic proportions (dhyana slokas).

title: Kalamezhuthu ritual floor drawing of Kerala
culturalContext: Kalamezhuthu is a sacred ritual visual tradition of Kerala where multidimensional representations of deities are drawn on consecrated temple floors using five natural powders: rice (white), turmeric (yellow), green leaves (green), burnt husk or charcoal (black), and a lime-turmeric blend (red). The ritual is performed by designated hereditary communities, including the Kurup and Theyyambadi families, accompanied by ritualistic singing known as Kalampattu, concluding with the ceremonial erasure of the drawing.

title: Kudiyattam — ancient Sanskrit temple theatre
culturalContext: Kudiyattam (literally 'acting together') is an ancient Sanskrit theatrical tradition native to Kerala with documented roots extending over eighteen hundred years. Traditionally staged within specialized temple theatres known as Koothambalams, Kudiyattam features sophisticated eye movements (netrabhinaya), codified hand gestures (mudras), and percussive accompaniment on the mizhavu drum. Recognized by UNESCO in 2001 as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity, it is preserved by hereditary Chakyar and Nambiar communities alongside contemporary performance institutions.

title: Kaikottikali — traditional folk dance of Kerala
culturalContext: Kaikottikali, also widely known as Thiruvathirakali, is a graceful community folk dance performed by women in Kerala during festive occasions, predominantly Onam and the winter festival of Thiruvathira. Dancing in circular formations around a lit brass oil lamp (nilavilakku), performers clad in traditional Kasavu attire clap their hands in rhythmic synchrony to melodic folk verses praising divine and heroic lore. The dance celebrates communal harmony, feminine grace, and seasonal agricultural renewal.

title: Kerala coir craft — traditional coconut fibre weaving
culturalContext: Coir craft is an integral traditional agro-cottage industry of coastal Kerala, centred in Alappuzha (Alleppey) and Kollam districts. Extracted from the fibrous outer husk of the coconut palm through natural water-retting in brackish lagoons, the golden fibres are spun into yarn using traditional two-wheel charkhas and hand-woven into mats, floor coverings, and nautical cordage. Kerala coir products hold Geographical Indication (GI) recognition, representing centuries of cooperative artisanal heritage and eco-friendly craftsmanship.
